transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m having a hard time staying with what I’m doing at work. On the floor, I’ll be dealing with a patient flow issue, and then an IV pump beeps or a call light goes off, or someone asks another nurse something… and I just lose the thread. I forget what I was in the middle of. It’s been happening a lot.
Is this difficulty with focusing and remembering what you were doing happening only at work or also in other parts of your life?

It’s not just work. It happens at home too… like I’ll mean to call someone back, or pay a bill, or I’ll set a reminder for an appointment and still somehow miss it. Even routine things just kind of slip.
Have you been feeling anxious or overwhelmed when these memory lapses happen?
I mean… I get frustrated, definitely. Overwhelmed maybe sometimes, but I don’t know if I’d call it anxious exactly. It’s more like, “how did I forget that again?” and then I try to move on.
How long have you been experiencing these memory lapses and difficulties with focusing?
It’s been… probably close to two years now. It got a lot more noticeable after I took on the expanded charge-nurse responsibilities. Since then it’s felt like a major problem.
Do you feel sad or depressed when these memory lapses happen?
Not really sad, no. Mostly just annoyed with myself… maybe embarrassed sometimes. I don’t think depressed is the word I’d use.
Did you have trouble paying attention or sitting still when you were a kid?

Yeah… I think so. I wasn’t really the kid who was constantly getting up, but in elementary school teachers would write that I was bright but careless. I lost worksheets a lot, forgot to turn in homework… that kind of thing. My mom had to sit with me most nights to keep me on track.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting, tapping your hands or feet, or feeling restless when you're sitting still?
I don’t think so… not in any obvious way. I might shift around a little, but I haven’t really noticed tapping or feeling like I can’t sit still.
Were you ever described as being overly active or having a lot of excess energy when you were a child?
Not really, no. I don’t remember being described that way. I was more… distracted, I guess, than overly energetic.
Do you ever find yourself becoming so focused on a task that you tune out everything else around you?
I’m not really sure. I mean… I can get into something sometimes, but I don’t know if I’d say I tune everything out. I haven’t paid much attention to that.
Do you ever become so absorbed in an activity that you lose track of time or forget about everything else around you?
I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t really notice that happening, or at least I can’t think of a clear example.
Have you noticed any significant improvement in your ability to focus when you're doing something that really interests you?
I’m not sure. Maybe a little sometimes, if it’s something I actually want to do, but I haven’t really noticed a big difference.
Can you think of any activities where you become so focused that you don't notice anything else around you?
Not really… I can’t think of anything specific where I’m that locked in. Maybe I just don’t notice it, but nothing comes to mind.
Do you ever find yourself becoming extremely focused on a task to the point where nothing else matters?
I don’t think so. I mean, not to that level. I can focus a bit more if something’s interesting, but “nothing else matters” doesn’t really sound like me.
Do you ever find yourself focusing on something so intensely that you don't even notice other people talking to you?
I don’t think so… not really. If someone’s talking to me, I usually notice, even if I’m distracted. I can’t think of a time where I was that absorbed.
Have these difficulties with focusing and remembering what you were doing significantly impacted your relationships with friends, family, or colleagues?

Yeah… at work, definitely. It’s gotten serious enough that I’m on formal supervision now, and some of the other nurses have to double-check parts of my follow-through when I’m charge. That’s been… hard. It makes me feel like I’m becoming more of a liability than a leader.
Have you noticed any significant differences in your ability to focus when you are in a quiet, distraction-free environment versus a busy, noisy one?

Yes. It’s definitely worse when it’s busy or noisy. On the floor, if an IV pump beeps, or a call light goes off, or someone asks another nurse something nearby, I just… lose what I was doing. Like I’ll be working through a patient flow issue and suddenly it’s gone. In a quiet space it’s not as bad.
Can you think of any specific tasks or activities where you feel you can focus without any difficulty?
I’m not sure. Nothing really comes to mind as something I can count on being easy to focus on. I guess if it’s very straightforward and quiet, maybe, but… I can’t think of a specific activity.
Have you felt like your difficulties with focusing and remembering what you were doing have caused you a lot of distress?

Yeah… it has. Mostly because of work. Being put on formal supervision and having other nurses double-check my follow-through when I’m charge… it’s embarrassing. It makes me feel like I’m not leading, like I’m becoming a liability.
Do you ever become so focused on something that you can't think of anything else?
Not really… I mean, I can get caught up in something for a little while, but I wouldn’t say it’s like I can’t think of anything else. I haven’t really noticed that.
Do you ever become completely absorbed in an activity, to the point where you're unaware of your surroundings?
I don’t think so. I mean, I can tune things out sometimes, but not completely unaware of what’s around me… at least not that I’ve noticed.
